ai_show_review.summary: Sunrise Montego Bay show shines with Scarlet>Fire and blazing Fire on the Mountain
ai_show_review.review: The November 26, 1982 Montego Bay gig is a rare Caribbean‑flavored gem that captures the Dead at a high‑energy peak. The sunrise second set delivers a smoking Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain sequence that many fans cite as the night’s centerpiece, while the first set builds momentum with a memorable Sugaree intro (complete with a cheeky Jamaican spoken lead‑in) and solid renditions of New Minglewood Blues and Althea.  Even though a few numbers—Althea → Let It Grow, Throwing Stones and a rushed Loser—don’t quite hit the mark, the overall flow stays tight, the band’s improvisational spark never wanes, and the tropical atmosphere adds an extra layer of vibe that makes this show stand out among ’82 dates.  Multiple pristine soundboard sources preserve every nuance, from Brent Mydland’s “rip‑in’ it” Hammond organ to Bill and Mickey’s tribal drum burst, giving listeners a clear window into one of the Dead’s most enjoyable festival performances.

best_recording.reason: Pristine soundboard capture with clear mix; includes the sunrise set’s iconic Scarlet>Fire and Fire on the Mountain, only a minor correctable speed issue.

key_highlights: Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain sunrise jam
Sugaree intro with Jamaican spoken lead‑in
High‑energy Fire on the Mountain and tight tribal drums
Caribbean vibe flowing through both sets, with strong organ textures

band_performance.Jerry: Emotive vocals and soaring guitar work; a bit weary on early Althea but fully ignites during Scarlet and Fire on the Mountain.
band_performance.Phil: Funky, present bass lines that lock in with Jerry; “Phil bombs” add extra groove throughout the set.
band_performance.Bob: Growl missing on Throwing Stones, but his harmonies shine on Not Fade Away and Black Peter, keeping the vocal blend rich.
band_performance.Keys: Brent delivers tremendous Hammond organ, crisp lead vocals, and an aggressive synth climax on Fire; organ‑guitar interplay is beautiful.
band_performance.Drums: Bill and Mickey provide tight, powerful drumming with a memorable tribal five‑minute drum segment and intense drive on Fire.
